formattedAddress: No. 47號, Emei St, Wanshou Village, Wanhua District, Taipei City, Taiwan 108

text.text: Recommended this restaurant by my dad as this place has been around since 1946. The sashimi and sushi here are very generous and and the prices are super affordable. Personally, the taste of the cuisine is different from what you'd get in Japan and more of a Taiwanese spin with some sweeter notes. I love the interior as it does have nostalgic vibes and the servers are nice as well.

text.text: During our visit in Taiwan. We visit them twice in our two weeks holiday. We tried their Sashimi rice bowl, their oyster dish. The sashimi was very fresh and portions were good. The cooked oyster dish was delicious and fresh as well. Very reasonable price and free miso soup with every order. Highly recommended.

text.text:
I don’t like to give a negative review for a place I do love to eat at. Let it be said I am fair in revisiting and seeing changes to restaurants over time. I have eaten here now four times over the last two years. The restaurant is busy attesting to their popularity in the XiMen neighborhood very near the metro. The food is tasty, and for the most part affordable, while they serve many more expensive dishes. I have found however that the sashimi I ordered, costing $NT700 ( my second time ever having it): the Toro Blue Fin Tuna Sashimi 7 piece includes thick pieces of sashimi, but two of the assortment is the fatty belly most desired sashimi and accounts for the price. It was however truly ONE PIECE SLICED TO HALF THE THICKNESS to provide you the two noted pieces of the seven in the assortment. Perhaps they are looking to higher profits or reduction of costs. It is notable that I was likewise served half a leaf is shiso with my sashimi— a dish costing over $US20 served with one leaf sliced in half and hidden under my half-cut Toro Maguro sashimi. The parallel presentation evoked a need to provide this FULL description. All other elements of my meal and experience was good and comfortable. I also had the baby abalone (under stir fry menu), conger eel nigiri was a generous whole butterfly cut of eel seven inches long! The uni nigiri sea urchin is fresh and comes with a chawan mushi steamed egg cup with clam and shrimp in it. My recommendation of the snowflake lily greens does not disappoint at $NT170 either— if they could just serve it WITH my meal vs. at the end when I literally was done with my meal and had to ask about it!
For value and variety their menu is incredible— but be warned you may be getting half-measures here. I recommend you eat here and just be aware.

In total I spent $US65 for one! I enjoy the food, but I cannot see a good place go bad… I hope this review encourages management to address changes that are noticeably reducing esteem.

text.text:
Very traditional Japanese restaurant since 1946.
The portions here are huge and affordable.
Big eaters will definitely be satisfied with the portions here.
Very fresh sashimi and sushi.
Well cooked dishes.
Lots of japanese food to choose from the menu.
Loved the miso soup here.
